body:
Fixes #8034

The C function of a `cpdef` method used its `skip_dispatch` argument as `skip_event` for the trace start. The Python wrapper passes 1 because it has already traced the call. But explicit calls like `Base.method(self, ...)` from Cython code also pass 1, without going through the wrapper, so they fired a return event but no call event. The reuse of `skip_dispatch` for this was added with the `sys.monitoring` support in #6144.

The wrapper now passes a separate value, 2, and the trace start skips the call event only for that value. Explicit base calls keep passing 1, so they still skip the override dispatch but are now traced. The three values are named in `Naming.py` (`cpdef_dispatch`, `cpdef_skip_dispatch`, `cpdef_wrapper_call`). `SimpleCallNode.cpdef_dispatch_mode()` computes which one a call passes.

Tests: `sys_monitoring.py` and the three `pstats_profile_test*` files now make explicit base calls to a plain method, a `noexcept` method with a C return type, and a method with an optional argument. All four test modules fail without the fix (`sys_monitoring` only on Python 3.12+) and pass with it on Python 3.11.12, 3.13.16 and 3.14.8.

Not addressed here, all on master too:
- With `Options.lookup_module_cpdef = True`, the module-level `cpdef` wrapper passes 0, so the call event fires twice.
- An explicit base call of a fused `cpdef` method generates C that doesn't compile.
- Converting an unbound `cpdef` method to a Python object (`fp = Base.m`) drops the `skip_dispatch` argument.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commit.message:
Fix missing trace call event for explicit base class calls of cpdef methods

The C implementation of a cpdef method used its "skip_dispatch" argument
also as "skip_event" for the profiling/tracing start event, assuming that
only the Python wrapper passes 1, which has already traced the call.
However, explicit non-virtual calls like "Base.method(self)" from Cython
code also pass 1 without going through the wrapper, so no call event was
emitted for them, only the return event.

The Python wrapper now passes 2 and only that value skips the call event.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Test more call variants of explicit cpdef base method calls and fix a C comment

Cover non-temp calls (C return type, noexcept) and vtable calls with
optional arguments in the tracing tests, in addition to the plain call.

The generated "Check if called by wrapper" comment no longer described
the dispatch check since explicit base type calls also skip the dispatch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Name the values of the cpdef "skip_dispatch" argument

Replace the bare 0/1/2 literals in the call code, the trace start code
and the signature adapting wrappers with shared constants in Naming.py.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Align the cpdef base call tracing tests with the surrounding tests

Mirror the new test cases into the pure Python and non-binding variants
of the pstats test, which keep the same set of methods, and move the
sys.monitoring test code into its own section in doctest order.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Pass the cpdef dispatch mode as a single argument

Instead of two booleans for one three-way value, compute the value of the
"skip_dispatch" argument once in SimpleCallNode.cpdef_dispatch_mode() and
pass it through build_c_call_code() and generate_cfunction_call().
The generated C code is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Use an enum for the values of the cpdef "skip_dispatch" argument

Move the values from Naming.py into a CpdefDispatch IntEnum next to
CFuncType, which declares the "skip_dispatch" argument.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
